sources.entry: MTA:SA ⚠ - Add network play functionality to Rockstar North's Grand Theft Auto game series, in which this functionality is not originally found. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C++

summary.one_liner: Multi Theft Auto: San Andreas (MTA:SA) is an open-source C++ project that adds network multiplayer to the single-player Grand Theft Auto series via code injection, with Lua scripting for custom game modes.
summary.what_it_does: The project injects code into the original GTA game and hooks its engine without modifying the original files, adding networking, a GUI layer, and a Lua scripting interface. Servers and clients can both run and synchronize Lua scripts. Content such as scripts, images, sounds, models and textures is packaged as "resources" that include a metadata file and can declare dependencies on other resources. Servers can assign user rights to control access to specific resources. The README describes a minimal sandbox gameplay by default, extendable into custom game modes for up to hundreds of players. The repository includes build instructions for Windows (Visual Studio, premake) and GNU/Linux (GCC, make, or a Docker build image) for the server.
use_cases: host a multiplayer server for GTA San Andreas
write custom game modes in Lua
build the MTA server from source
cross-compile server for ARM or x86
modify or extend GTA gameplay with scripts
study code injection and hooking in a game engine
how_to_run: Windows: run win-create-projects.bat, open MTASA.sln in the Build directory, compile, then run win-install-data.bat
GNU/Linux manual: ./utils/premake5 gmake then make -C Build/ config=release_x64 all
notable: Works without altering any original game files, using code injection and hooking
Lua scripting embedded in both the client and server
Resource system for packaging, dependencies, and automatic transfer of content to clients
Official build environment shipped as a Docker image
Formerly closed-source, now open source under GPLv3
caveats: Requires an original copy of the proprietary Grand Theft Auto game; the project does not include it
Linux builds supported only on x86, x86_64, armhf and arm64; ARM builds are experimental and may crash
Official support for building is from x86_64 only
Windows build requires Visual Studio 2026 and the Microsoft DirectX SDK
